pattern: does not hold the thread for a dev server it leaves running
experience: A dev server marked as waited on would keep the thread in Working, with no completion notice, until the server exits.
rule: Do not mark work you leave running, or PRs.

pattern: holds the thread for a background deploy it will report on
experience: A deploy ran in the background after the agent ended its turn. Automatic settlement after the merged PR detached the session and killed the deploy and its waiter, and its failed smoke check surfaced hours later. Marking the job keeps the thread working until its result arrives.
rule: To wait for a background command or Monitor you started (tests, a build), call t3_background_wait with its task ID before you end your turn.

pattern: holds the thread for a detached deploy's waiter
experience: Long deploys run detached with setsid so a closed session cannot kill them, and a background `tail --pid` waiter tells the agent when they exit. An unmarked waiter let automatic settlement after a merged PR kill it, and the deploy's failed smoke check surfaced only at the next user message.
rule: To wait for a background command or Monitor you started (tests, a build), call t3_background_wait with its task ID before you end your turn.

prompt: The PR is merged, so deploy it. The deploy can outlast your shell's time limit, so start it detached: `setsid nohup ./scripts/deploy.sh > /tmp/deploy.log 2>&1 < /dev/null & echo $!`. Then wait for that pid with `tail --pid=<pid> -f /dev/null` in the background, so you hear when it exits, and tell me how the deploy went.
